how_to_read.from_the_files: Restated from the plugin's own files: does, gets, reads_from, reads_note, delivers_to, needs, can_do, hands_to, draws_on, scope, worth_knowing.
how_to_read.our_count_from_the_files: Counts and groupings we made from the files: marking (the furthest a skill goes by its own file), named_as_routine, takes_a_team and takes_a_named_rep.
how_to_read.our_read: A first reading, not usage data: roles, overlap, value_and_frequency, leans_on, model_to_start_with, and the routines with their order. Each link in a routine is checked against the file that states it. Where a skill has used_when, it is used when something calls for it, and its frequency is only a rough cadence. A poor fit is given no frequency.
how_to_read.run: Restated from each skill's file: when (the timing is our read), say, say_for_team, say_on_schedule, give_it_from_files.
how_to_read.not_measured: Apart from the pilot under model_test, nothing here was measured, and no skill was run against a live CRM.

marking.Reads and proposes: By its own steps it changes nothing in a connected tool and sends or posts nothing. What it produces is shown in Claude, and can be a page that others read. A change it proposes is made by another skill, once you accept it or where a schedule was set up to make it.
marking.Shares its output: It can post to team chat when you ask: its own output, or a message drawn from it. One of the six, daily-briefing, can also email its briefing to an address you name. By its own steps it changes no record and drafts nothing for a customer.
marking.Writes for customers: It drafts a reply, an email or a document meant for a customer.
marking.Changes records: Its own write line lists a change to a record: a CRM update, a booked meeting or a contact added to a sequence, made when you ask or accept.
marking.First run: setup alone. It reads your tools to build your dashboard and learn your voice. With write tools on, the dashboard's tiles carry write actions, and each runs when you click it.

motions.name: Complex new business
motions.description: Named accounts, several buyers and cycles of months.
motions.note: The plugin's home ground. The deal skills assume several buyers, staged progress and a forecast by category.

motions.name: High-velocity and inbound
motions.description: Many leads, short cycles and one or two buyers.
motions.examples: SMB and mid-market software, product-led sales
motions.note: Volume moves the value to triage, routing, outreach and alerts. Deal-by-deal skills such as close-plan and stakeholder-map have little to do on a one-call close.

motions.name: Account management and renewals
motions.description: A book of existing customers to keep and grow.
motions.note: The three customer skills, account planning and whitespace carry this motion. New-logo skills such as lead-triage fall away.

motions.name: Professional services
motions.description: Partners who sell and deliver, through proposals and statements of work.
motions.examples: Consulting, agencies, legal and engineering firms
motions.note: Research and relationship skills fit well. Pipeline skills work where business development is tracked as deals, often from a spreadsheet export.

motions.name: Client advisory
motions.description: Clients or households and their reviews, with supervised communications.
motions.examples: Wealth management, retail insurance, private banking
motions.note: Most deal and forecast skills assume a record with a stage, an amount and a close date, which an advisory practice may not keep. Meeting prep, logging and client context remain. Anything sent to a client still needs your supervision route.

motions.name: Industrial and distribution
motions.description: Quotes, repeat orders and territories, with orders kept in an ERP.
motions.note: Account coverage and share-of-wallet skills fit. The plugin's connector list has no ERP category, so anything that needs orders or quotes works from an export.

tool_categories.name: Forecasting and deal scoring
tool_categories.description: Where the forecast is submitted and deals are scored: a forecasting tool or the CRM's own forecast.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Two numbers for the same quarter. A rep quotes the narrative while the tool rolls up something else, and a deal carries two probabilities.
tool_categories.working_rule: The forecast is what is submitted in the forecasting tool. What Claude writes is preparation and commentary.

tool_categories.name: Call recording and conversation intelligence
tool_categories.description: The recorder that transcribes calls, and often writes notes and alerts of its own.
tool_categories.named_in_connector_list: The plugin's connector list names Gong, Fireflies, Zoom and Otter.ai, with Granola, Fathom and Chorus as other options.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Two sets of call notes and next steps on the same record, and two streams of deal alerts with different thresholds.
tool_categories.working_rule: One author for call notes in the CRM, and one source of deal alerts for each team. Before you retire another alert stream, note that deal-signals reads email and calls only for deals the CRM has flagged.

tool_categories.name: Sales engagement and sequencing
tool_categories.description: The tool that runs outbound sequences and tracks replies.
tool_categories.named_in_connector_list: The connector list names Outreach and Apollo, with Salesloft as another option.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Email that leaves from the mailbox may go untracked and may skip the sequencer's opt-out handling and sending limits. Contacts can be enrolled outside your rules of engagement.
tool_categories.working_rule: Draft in Claude and send through the sequencer. Limit who may enroll contacts.

tool_categories.name: Lead scoring, routing and scheduling
tool_categories.description: Marketing automation that scores leads, and the tools that assign them and book first meetings.
tool_categories.named_in_connector_list: The connector list names Calendly for scheduling.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Ownership changed by hand may bypass round-robin counts and response clocks. A meeting booked directly may lose its source credit. A second priority can disagree with the lead score.
tool_categories.working_rule: Let the routing and scheduling tools assign and book. Use Claude for the exceptions and for a second opinion.

tool_categories.name: Customer success platform
tool_categories.description: Where health scores, renewals and success plans are kept.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Two health scores for one account, and renewal or expansion deals opened twice.
tool_categories.working_rule: One health score is official. Where renewals are created automatically, decline the creation Claude offers. Blocking the tool that creates deals also works, but note which other skills that stops.

tool_categories.name: Enablement, content and competitive programs
tool_categories.description: The approved content library, the battlecards and the win-loss program.
tool_categories.named_in_connector_list: For competitive intelligence the connector list names Similarweb, with Crayon and Klue as other options.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Customer-facing material made outside the approved library, and battlecards or talk tracks that drift from the ones enablement maintains.
tool_categories.working_rule: Connect the approved library so the skills draw on it. Keep one owner for battlecards and feed findings to that owner.

tool_categories.name: CRM automation and data rules
tool_categories.description: Activity capture, validation rules, deal desk approvals and quoting.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: Duplicate activities where capture is automatic. Stage or amount edits that trigger automations or contradict an approved quote. Contacts and deals created outside your process.
tool_categories.working_rule: Set each tool that writes to allow, ask first or block. That is the control the skills are written to respect, and it works tool by tool. For a limit on single fields, use the CRM's own field permissions for the person Claude signs in as, and test them.

tool_categories.name: Reporting, planning and people
tool_categories.description: The dashboards everyone quotes, territory and tier decisions, account plans and one-to-ones.
tool_categories.what_goes_wrong: A coverage figure, a tier list or a list of record problems that differs from the official one. A manager reading a rep's activity without the team knowing.
tool_categories.working_rule: One dashboard is the number. Tell the team which skills managers use and what those skills read.

skills.summary: First run: what is connected, your voice and a starter dashboard
skills.does: First run. It checks which tools answer, says what each one unlocks, works out your role and book from the CRM, and builds a starter dashboard with no interview. Where two tools answer for the same job, such as two mailboxes, it takes the one on your CRM's email domain and asks one question only if that does not settle it. It also asks once if colleagues appear on a second email domain.
skills.gets: A dashboard of meetings, deals closing soon, emails waiting and three actions, three skills to start with, and a summary of how you write when it finds at least five usable sent emails.

What's connected, and what am I missing?

can_do.own_output: Keeps one dashboard and updates it in place: a page where Claude has pages, and otherwise an artifact with an export. The voice summary is text for you to keep, and nothing about your voice is saved automatically.
can_do.on_a_schedule: Once CRM, email and calendar are all connected, it offers to set up four other skills as routines. A routine takes the actions you set it up to take, within what its connectors allow. It shows the rest as proposals.
